clinicalPearls: The ABCDE criteria guide clinical suspicion: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variegation, Diameter > 6 mm, and Evolution/change
Breslow thickness is the single most important histological prognostic factor for primary cutaneous melanoma
Superficial spreading melanoma is the most common subtype in light-skinned populations, frequently associated with intermittent intense sun exposure
Acral lentiginous melanoma occurs on palms, soles, and subungual sites, and has similar incidence across all racial groups independent of UV exposure
Excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin is the diagnostic standard; wide local excision margins depend strictly on Breslow depth
Sentinel lymph node biopsy is offered for intermediate-thickness melanomas (stage pT1b or greater) to guide staging and adjuvant systemic therapy
Targeted therapies (BRAF and MEK inhibitors for BRAF V600 mutations) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1, anti-CTLA-4) form the backbone of advanced disease management
reference.pathophysiology: Cutaneous melanoma arises from malignant transformation of melanocytes located in the basal layer of the epidermis. Ultraviolet radiation, particularly episodic severe sunburns, induces DNA photoproducts and mutations in critical regulatory genes including BRAF (most frequently V600E), NRAS, and CDKN2A/p16. Tumour progression evolves from radial growth phase (intraepidermal or microinvasive) to vertical growth phase (dermal infiltration), correlating with metastatic competence and worsening prognosis.
additionalDifferentials: Benign melanocytic naevus or dysplastic naevus
Subungual haematoma (moves distally with nail growth)
additionalInvestigations: Dermoscopy evaluation (pigment network, atypical dots/globules, blue-white veil)
Complete surgical excision biopsy with 2 mm margin and full-thickness subcutaneous fat for formal histological staging
Histopathology report specifying Breslow thickness, ulceration status, mitotic rate, and peripheral/deep margins
Sentinel lymph node biopsy for pT1b or higher disease
Molecular testing for BRAF V600 mutation in metastatic or high-risk resected disease
Staging imaging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, PET-CT, MRI brain) for advanced disease
